title: Indices, Logarithm and Surds Quiz 5
description: What a logarithm is, and its special values.
instructions: Indices, Logarithm and Surds: Meaning of a logarithm.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Find $\log_2 64$.
questions.explanation: $2^{6}=64$, so $\log_2 64=6$. Watch out: the answer is the exponent $6$, not the base $2$.

questions.question: What is $\log_{10}100$?
questions.explanation: $10^2=100$, so the logarithm is $2$. Watch out: the logarithm is the power, not the number $100$.

questions.question: $\log_b 1=0$ for every valid base $b$.
questions.explanation: $b^0=1$ for every base, so $\log_b1=0$. Watch out: this holds for every allowed base, not just $10$.

questions.question: Which is the exponential form of $\log_3 27=3$?
questions.explanation: $\log_b a=y$ means $b^{y}=a$, so $3^{3}=27$. Watch out: the base of the logarithm stays the base of the power.

questions.question: $\log_b 0=0$.
questions.explanation: No power of $b$ gives $0$, so $\log_b0$ is undefined. Watch out: it is not $0$ and not a number at all.

questions.question: Find $\ln e^{5}$.
questions.explanation: $\ln$ is $\log_e$, so $\ln e^{5}=5$. Watch out: $\ln$ has base $e$, not $10$.

questions.question: The common logarithm is the logarithm to which base?
questions.explanation: $\log x$ means $\log_{10}x$. Watch out: base $e$ is the natural logarithm, written $\ln x$.

questions.question: Find $\log_5 5$.
questions.explanation: $5^{1}=5$, so $\log_55=1$. Watch out: $\log_b b=1$, not $0$ (that is $\log_b1$).

questions.question: Solve $\log_2 x=5$.
questions.explanation: Write it as a power: $x=2^{5}=32$. Watch out: $x=2\times5=10$ is the usual slip.

questions.question: Match each logarithm with its value.
questions.explanation: $2^3=8$, $3^2=9$, $10^0=1$ and $5^1=5$. Watch out: $\log_{10}1$ is $0$, because any base to the power $0$ is $1$.
